artifacts.summary: Root-cause analysis of the CLAUDE.md double-body and settings.json duplicate Stop-hook defects, with a recommended fix confined to sync.lua's reinject_loaded_extensions() and merge.lua's deep_merge().

memory_candidates.content: This nvim agent-system repo's CLAUDE.md/OPENCODE.md merge targets (merge_target_key claudemd/opencode_md) moved to a fully-computed-artifact regeneration model (generate_claudemd() in shared/extensions/merge.lua, called from shared/extensions/init.lua's load/unload paths) that deliberately writes NO <!-- SECTION: id --> markers -- this superseded an earlier section-injection model. Any code path that still calls merge_mod.inject_section() for the claudemd/opencode_md merge key (as claude/commands/picker/operations/sync.lua's reinject_loaded_extensions() does) will append a stray duplicate copy on every run, since the markerless file never satisfies inject_section()'s idempotency check.

merge.lua's deep_merge() dedups array items via whole-item vim.deep_equal, not matcher-aware merging. For Claude Code settings.json hook-event arrays (Stop, PreToolUse, etc.), this means a source fragment declaring a hook as its own separate {matcher, hooks} block will never dedup against an existing differently-shaped matcher block containing the same hook command bundled with others -- it gets appended as a new block, duplicating the hook registration. The core manifest.json's own _comment on merge_targets.settings already documents this as a known, unfixed risk.
